The stimulation or manipulation of these events by electronic means provides the opportunity for unique control and experimentation that are orthogonal to existing biochemical or genetic approaches. Devices All devices on the fire alarm system shall be compatible with Apollo XP95 protocol. Tender Document r5d_V4.8_ENE_GenC4.8 (Supply) Photoelectric Smoke Detectors The primary fire detection on the system shall be by means of analogue addressable photoelectric type smoke detectors. Devices shall be fitted onto an addressable base. Detectors are to be easily replaceable without tools, and, when mounted at height, allow testing and replacement using an extension tool. Heat Detectors Heat detectors shall be of the rate of rise type or combination type (Heat / Smoke) They shall use the same base as the smoke detectors. Indoor / Outdoor Manual Call Points These shall be of the indoor flush or surface type. The units shall have the following characteristics: Device Type: Manual Call Point supplied with plastic cover Operating Principle: Breaking of glass causes switch to change state Sampling Frequency: Continuous Alarm Indicator: Red light emitting diode IP Rating (minimum): IPx4 Indoor IP66 Outdoor All call points shall use a non—frangible element which is resettable using a special key.

Introduction/Background This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for the depot-level maintenance and repair of the NATO Seasparrow system components listed in Section 6. The objective of this SOW is to ensure the reliable and cost-effective repair of these components to CODE A condition, ready for issue, in accordance with the references located in Section 2. The work described herein is critical to maintaining the operational readiness and availability of the NATO Seasparrow system. 1.0 Scope The scope of this SOW encompasses all actions required to perform depot-level repair on the electronic components listed in Section 6. This includes, but is not limited to, receiving inspection, disassembly, cleaning, inspection, repair, replacement of parts, reassembly, testing, marking, and packaging according to the applicable Technical Repair Standard (TRS). In the absence of a TRS, the contractor may conduct the repair in accordance with locally generated procedures.
